name: Floss

card.summary: String for cleaning between teeth: recommended by dental associations, with systematic reviews rating the evidence low certainty.
card.note: Guidelines changed in 2015 US dietary guidance omission; ADA continues to recommend daily use.

quick.overview:
Dental floss is thread or tape used to clean between teeth. The American Dental Association recommends flossing once a day, and it is routine in dental advice. It appears in looksmaxxing lists as basic teeth upkeep.

Systematic reviews have judged the evidence that adding floss to brushing improves plaque or gingivitis to be low to very low certainty.
quick.mechanism: Floss mechanically disrupts plaque on surfaces a toothbrush misses. Types include waxed or unwaxed nylon or silk, tape, picks, threaders and powered flossers.
quick.risks: Misuse can cut gums or cause finger circulation problems if wrapped too tightly, and fibres can catch on dental work.

lead: Dental floss is a thread, usually nylon or silk, used to clean between the teeth. It comes waxed or unwaxed, monofilament or multifilament, with tape, picks, threaders and powered flossers as alternatives [1]. The American Dental Association recommends daily flossing before or after brushing [1].

Evidence is mixed. A 2011 Cochrane review found some evidence that flossing reduces gingivitis but weak evidence for plaque reduction, and a 2019 Cochrane review of interdental cleaning devices rated the evidence as low to very low certainty [1][2]. The 2015 US Dietary Guidelines dropped the flossing recommendation, which an August 2016 Associated Press article reported; HHS said it was not questioning efficacy [1].
infobox: World War II, Charles C. Bass [1]

paras: Levi Spear Parmly recommended waxed silk thread in 1819. Unwaxed silk floss became commercially available in 1882 from Codman and Shurtleff, Johnson & Johnson received a patent in 1898, and nylon floss was developed by Charles C. Bass during World War II. Flossing became routine in the US and Canada in the 1970s [1].

A 2008 systematic review found flossing added to brushing no more effective than brushing alone for plaque or gingivitis, while a 2006 review of school programs with professional flossing found a 40% reduction in decay risk [1]. The 2019 Cochrane review covers home use of interdental cleaning devices for periodontal disease and caries [2].
Misuse can cause gum cuts, finger circulation problems if wrapped too tightly, and fibres catching on appliances [1].
A Cochrane review examined home use of interdental cleaning devices in addition to toothbrushing and judged evidence low certainty [2]. No studies found examining floss for facial appearance.

timeline.event: Levi Spear Parmly recommends waxed silk thread [1].
Unwaxed silk floss commercially available from Codman and Shurtleff [1].
Johnson & Johnson receives a floss patent [1].
AP reports the flossing recommendation was dropped from the 2015 US Dietary Guidelines [1].
